excerpt: Nomagic is a Polish company making AI-powered robots for warehouse picking, packing and sorting. Funding, customers and alternatives.
content:
Nomagic is a Warsaw-based robotics company that builds AI-driven robotic arms for warehouses. Its robots pick individual items, pack them and sort them, jobs that are hard to automate because products vary so much in shape and packaging. Its site now describes this as physical AI for end-to-end warehouse automation in the world's most complex warehouses. Tech.eu reported that the systems include 24/7 AI-based monitoring and a remote operations platform, so a small team can keep many robots running around the clock.

The company was started in 2017 by Kacper Nowicki, its chief executive, Marek Cygan and Tristan d'Orgeval. It serves retailers, e-commerce distributors, manufacturers and third-party logistics providers; customer logos on its site include ASOS, Arvato, Brack.Alltron, apo.com and BestSecret.

In February 2025 Nomagic raised a $44 million Series B led by the venture arm of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, with existing investors Khosla Ventures and Almaz Capital, including venture debt previously signed with the European Investment Bank. The EBRD said its money would support product development, sales and marketing, and Nowicki said the plan was to expand deployments across Europe over two years. Startup press reported a further $10 million Series B extension in early 2026 led by Cogito Capital Partners, bringing total funding to over $84 million, aimed at growth in the US and work on vision-language-action models.

Nomagic does not publish prices. Warehouse robots are usually sold through a project that starts with a site assessment; buyers should ask about pricing models such as robot-as-a-service versus purchase.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
